accuracy.evidence: Checked for a card: To and the reader's name as the greeting, one message that fits the reason, Love from or From with the writer's own name as the sign-off, names with a capital letter, and the reader's name on the envelope; matched to Development Matters 2021 Reception Literacy, the EYFS 2024 ELG Writing and NC England Year 1 and 2 Writing composition (say it aloud first, write for different purposes).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real early-writing slips: own name after To, From at the top, a message that does not fit the picture, Love from at the top or with the other person's name, To at the bottom, the sender's name on the envelope, and a name with no capital, each in the adult text and in the lab replies.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is a card with three writing places and an envelope: tags are dragged to the top, middle or bottom of real cards, messages onto the card whose picture they fit, and finished cards into the envelope whose name matches To; the mechanism is the layout of a card and cannot be relabelled for another topic.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner places each part and the card shows the result: the wrong To tag lights the top line red with the reason (that is your own name), the wrong place for Love from says the top is for To, and the built card then reads To Dad, the message, Love from Mia from top to bottom.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: Sam's own name after To, Love from at the top of the card, and the maker's name on the envelope; each step then shows the right place and the reply that disproves the wrong choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions with slip-tagged wrong options (self, word, fit, who, word2, mid, env, other, cap, place); for example choosing Leo for the envelope replies that is the name of the person who made it, the envelope gets the name after To.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and the words on the card itself (To, Love from, Happy birthday, Get well soon) and passes the kid readability limit; adult text explains the curriculum links and key words in plain language.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one part of a card (what a card is for, the top, the middle, the bottom and envelope); adult paragraphs cover the EYFS goal, the NC link, the common mistakes and the lab, with no throat-clearing.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark themes: the card fills the width with readable lines, the tags stack in one column as full-width 44 px targets, the three envelopes and picture cards fit side by side, and nothing is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button path: pick a tag button, then a place, card or envelope button, with aria-pressed on the held tag; the canvas aria-label follows each reply; walk.cjs reports axe clean in both themes on desktop and phone with every Show me task completing.
